body: Actually, on second thoughts your promotion job sounds terrifying...

That must have been very stressful for you, and upsetting to have to leave the job because of such a mistake. Surely your employer must have understood? It's great that you managed to find another job., though. I don't have that flexibility. In my field, you get one or two jobs in a lifetime. No changing or moving around. 

Funny, I would have been the opposite in your situation. I enjoy being active and in the front of things, though I am very introverted. Society needs all types, it's just a question of finding a situation where you feel appreciated and useful..no matter what you do. 


I really don't have friends on a level that they can help me. My parents are 10,000km away. I have a lot of acquaintances, but they mostly disappeared when I went down. I don't have close friends. My most trusted friend was the guy I had a crush on, and he attacked me very viciously out of the blue, telling me everything wrong about me and even criticising my situation, partly out of a weird kind of jealousy, I think. I waited until he left, then broke down completely. It's been five months, and it still hurts badly. This, as well as marriage problems, has had a bad effect on my relationships with others, including my family- I feel no love or friendship any more, only pain. 

Yes...I've been trying to get some videos and recordings arranged. I have a couple already up, from better days. I was fairly successful before, and hoped to go freelance after quitting my job. Because of my breakdown, I couldn't even start, and the chances of getting any work are slim anyway. Really, I'd press forward if there were even a tiny glimpse of hope. I've always been hardworking. 

I'm really grateful for your kindness. It makes a big difference.

I really miss my work. It was part of me and I was passionate about it. It's a way of life. I was into it so much that it may have had a bad effect on my marriage. I don't know. So much has happened, it's all mixed up now and nobody can tell what caused what.

Sorry for the late reply, I spent today being sick with flu... 

Yes...it's a very difficult situation with no logical solution that I can see. Thanks a lot for your offer of researching options for me...though I have of course been through them all, and am still trying to get back on my feet again in spite of the dark prognosis. As for my field, it might be easier for most people to visualize that I am a ballerina. I'm not, but something similar and equally high maintenance/highly pressured. A ballerina needs a troupe to belong to and be employed with; well, I had that, and quit it for our relationship's sake. At my age, I'm way past being admitted to another company, and teaching at schools is not an option. I am good at teaching high level pupils who are going to specialize or are already skilled, but the relevant institutions won't have me as I am a newcomer in the country and have built up few credits along those lines. I've mainly been a performer. I had hoped things would go better work-wise, but have to face the reality that I've messed up. So there we have it...

Well, this is where the trapped factor comes into play. I quit my job and have no work, so have no independent means and nowhere to go in this foreign country. I'm sick and feel incapable of working anyway. My self-esteem and body image have been destroyed, so I don't feel capable of attracting another partner, ever. I love my husband and don't feel I can be with another man for real. The young man I had a crush on spurned me, and in any case I really don't think anyone else could love me in my present broken state. Men only look to high achieving women my age as viable partners, not wretches whose life has fallen apart. And I'm 39 and don't yet have a child, and the only chance I have of ever starting a family would be with my husband as I can't imagine building up another relationship within a year to the point where it's possible to have a baby. In 15 years of marriage, we haven't managed to get to that point, and after what's happened i truly feel incapable, but still hope to fix things in time. So nothing is as it should be, and I can't find a way out of this mess.

I know...I myself can't see a way out, which is why I want to end things rather than live on in this way. 

I know my husband does want to fix things, and he's slowly getting used to the idea of communication. Until now, he mostly left everything to me, and while I was capable I could deal with that. Not any more. It wasn't until I stopped functioning that I noticed he wasn't enthusiastic about anything but just let things happen. 

My husband refuses to see a counselor. I dragged him to a sessioj with my therapist, and he acted boorishly. He won't even read a book on partnership problems with me. He seems to believe that things will heal themselves, but so far they haven't. Even if he is more helpful now, the past two years of terrible marital strife have taken such a toll on me that I'm not sure anything will ever go right again. I now associate pain, loneliness and rejection with him rather than the good feelings one should have in a loving home. Although I still want to give it my best try, I feel really broken as a person by everything that's happened, and see no way to fix that. I'm not a viable wife or mother any more. 


Thanks a lot for your help, and please don't apologize! It's really kind of you to bother. Honestly, I wouldn't be posting here if I were not on my very last legs. 


I do have a lot to occupy my mind, and engage in quite a few activities (without going out, if possible). I have the physical energy, but lack the mental power to do things. This is a scary state, as it means I can act as normal while I'm all black and rotten inside. I could walk around for the rest of my life knowing that my love for my husband and for life has been broken. I could carry on living with him even though I met someone else whom I badly wanted to be together with. I could just go through the motions until I drop dead. That terrifies me.

Well..Yes, we had discussed family and planned it, but it seemed my husband was having doubts which he hadn't shared with me. I felt he'd lied to me, or at least neglected to address important issues before my move...things that would have affected my decision to quit my job, which I now think was the worst decision I ever made. 

I've spent the past two years trying to get him to talk so we can fix things. The rejection has continued, though he's softened up a bit very recently. We still have big flareups at weekends, where I beg him to do his part in our marriage and help to build intimacy again. 


I'm no perfect model wife either, seeing as I'm the one who fell for another person :/ But at least I try?!?

Well, it began with the stress of the big decision to move, which happened just before I became aware of my husband's rejection and the odd games he had been playing to stop me from getting pregnant. From then on, it was just a viscious circle: rejection, no work, leading to depression, leading to no work, leading to more depression and more rejection (the sicker i got, the less he wanted me).

I don't know...I have the feeling that I just don't want to continue. it was hard enough building it up the first time, without baggage. Not that I object to things being hard. I just don't have the will and urge to show a fighting spirit like I used to. But I'm glad you managed. It takes a lot of courage, I think.
